column1: # CA keys a bundled trust store or pin must not rely on, matched by SubjectPublicKeyInfo
# SHA-256 (the hash NSPinnedDomains/TrustKit pins use), so cross-signed and reissued copies
# of a certificate match too. Every certificate SHA-256 was recomputed from the DER served by
# crt.sh or curl's Mozilla extract (curl.se/ca) and checked against the cited source.
# Format: SPKI SHA-256 (base64) <TAB> kind <TAB> name <TAB> certificate SHA-256s <TAB> sources <TAB> SPKI DER (base64)
# The SPKI DER finds keys compiled in as raw bytes (DER arrays, BearSSL trust anchors).
# Kinds: compromised = private key is public (eMudhra P-384 keys are integers below 256; the
#   d·G unit test in src/resources/weak_ec.rs proves each); issuer = CA that issued the
#   compromised intermediates; cross-signer = still-trusted root that cross-signed them;
#   distrusted = removed from Mozilla's root store for CA compliance failures.
# eMudhra incident: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2083449 (all 8 keys recovered; Sectigo cross-signs affected).
